assumptions.condition: \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_x>0\) and \(m(x)>0\).

standard.name: Strong sign-separation variant for covariate-specific selection direction

definitions.name: Tie-safe survivor-complier model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ satisfies conditional instrument independence, treatment consistency, treatment-mediated selection and outcome exclusion, instrument overlap, no defiers, latent-direction weak selection monotonicity, and positive aggregate survivor-complier mass}\}\).  This is the finite-ordered, finite-covariate specialization of Dong--Heiler Assumptions 3.1--3.2 on cells with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\); cells with \(P(C\mid X=x)=0\) have zero capacities and are inert for the target.

definitions.name: Margin-free uniform inference law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P\in\mathcal M:P\text{ satisfies the uniform aggregate-survivor and independent-sampling conditions at index }n\}\).  No selection-direction separation condition is imposed.

definitions.name: Observable selected-complier capacities
definitions.construction: For \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), form \(\ell_i(x)\) and \(h_j(x)\) from the two conditional instrument contrasts displayed in the symbol table, set \(q_0(x)=\sum_i\ell_i(x)\), \(q_1(x)=\sum_jh_j(x)\), define \(\Delta q(x)=q_1(x)-q_0(x)\), and set \(m(x)=\min\{q_0(x),q_1(x)\}\).

definitions.name: Branch-free exact-mass partial-transport polytope
definitions.construction:
\[\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x),\ \sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij,x}=m(x)\right\}.\]
For comparison, retain
\[\Gamma_x^{+}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x)\right\},\qquad
\Gamma_x^{-}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\},\]
and
\[\Gamma_x^{0}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\}.\]
Define \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).

definitions.name: Closed threshold-cut endpoints
definitions.construction:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), define
\[
B_L(x)=\max\left\{0,\ \max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)\bigr]+\min\{\Delta q(x),0\}\right\}
\]
and
\[
B_U(x)=\min\left\{m(x),\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)\bigr]\right\}.
\]
These formulas are branch-free and remain defined on positive-survivor zero-gap cells and on zero-survivor cells.

definitions.name: Threshold-flow and latent-completion construction
definitions.construction: In each cell, first compute the exact mass \(m(x)\), the prefix and tail sums, and the two threshold values.  For an upper-attaining coupling, greedily construct a maximum subflow on the nested benefit graph \(i<j\); for a lower-attaining coupling, greedily construct a maximum subflow on the nested nonbenefit graph \(j\le i\).  Complete either subflow to total mass \(m(x)\) by a two-pointer allocation on the residual complete bipartite graph.  The result belongs to \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).  Allocate every row or column residual to the one-sided selected-complier stratum forced by the sign of \(q_1(x)-q_0(x)\), put the remaining compliers in the never-selected stratum, and adjoin the unchanged never-taker and always-taker components of a baseline compatible law.

definitions.name: Fully specified three-level observed and latent witness
definitions.construction: Let \(X=x^{\star}\) almost surely, \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=1)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=0)=1/2\), and \(K=3\). Given \(Z=0\), assign probabilities \(0.075\), \(0.10\), and \(0.075\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,1,0),(0,1,1),(0,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.75\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,0,\star)\). Given \(Z=1\), assign probabilities \(0.10\), \(0.25\), and \(0.15\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,1,0),(1,1,1),(1,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.50\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,0,\star)\); all unlisted conditional cells have probability zero. Construct \(P^{\star}\) by taking every unit to satisfy \(D_0=0,D_1=1\), allocating masses \(0.075,0.10,0.075\) to \(S_0=S_1=1\) with diagonal survivor pairs \((Y_0,Y_1)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)\), allocating mass \(0.25\) to \(S_0=0,S_1=1\) with \(Y_1\) residual masses \((0.025,0.15,0.075)\), and allocating mass \(0.50\) to \(S_0=S_1=0\). Take \(Z\) independent with probability one half and assign arbitrary latent outcomes wherever selection makes them unobserved.

definitions.name: Total constrained plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction:
For every empirical conditional probability given \((X=x,Z=z)\), use its empirical ratio when the denominator is positive and the fixed value zero when the denominator is zero. Form \(\widetilde c_n=(\widetilde\ell,\widetilde h)\), set \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), and define \(\widehat c_n=\Pi_{\mathfrak C}(\widetilde c_n)=\arg\min_{c\in\mathfrak C}\|c-\widetilde c_n\|_2^2\). The fixed Euclidean metric makes the minimizer unique, and \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\) is the coordinatewise positive-part map. From \(\widehat c_n=(\widehat\ell,\widehat h)\), form \(\widehat q_0(x)=\sum_i\widehat\ell_i(x)\), \(\widehat q_1(x)=\sum_j\widehat h_j(x)\), \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)=\widehat q_1(x)-\widehat q_0(x)\), and \(\widehat m(x)=\min\{\widehat q_0(x),\widehat q_1(x)\}\). Evaluate
\[
\widehat B_L(x)=\max\left\{0,\ \max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\left[\sum_{i\le t}\widehat\ell_i(x)-\sum_{j\le t}\widehat h_j(x)\right]+\min\{\widehat{\Delta q}(x),0\}\right\}
\]
and
\[
\widehat B_U(x)=\min\left\{\widehat m(x),\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\left[\sum_{i<t}\widehat\ell_i(x)+\sum_{j>t}\widehat h_j(x)\right]\right\}.
\]
Set \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), retain exactly the cells satisfying \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\), and form \(\widehat M_n=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), \(\widehat N_{L,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_L(x)\), and \(\widehat N_{U,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_U(x)\). Define \(\widehat\Psi_n=(\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n)\) when \(\widehat M_n>0\), and use the fixed fallback \(\widehat\Psi_n=(0,1)\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Conservative guarded inference and face diagnostic
definitions.construction:
Use the same retained-cell rule \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\).  The near-active lower and upper threshold cuts, the active face of \(\min\{\widehat{\Delta q}(x),0\}\), the active face of \(\min\{\widehat q_0(x),\widehat q_1(x)\}\), and the coordinatewise nonnegativity faces generated by \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\) define a computable finite diagnostic face envelope for \(\mathbb G_n^\xi\).  This multiplier envelope is not used as a calibrated critical value in the present uniform theorem.  Set \(a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\) and
\[
g_n=\frac{512K|\mathcal X|}{m_{\star}\varepsilon_Z^2}(a_n+\eta_n).
\]
Define the conservative guarded confidence set
\[
\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}=
\left[\max\{0,\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_n\},\ \min\{1,\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_n\}\right].
\]
The deterministic guard supplies uniform containment; first-order exact calibration of an unguarded face-aware multiplier region remains outside this construction.

statements.statement: For every supported \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), \(\ell_i(x)=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and \(h_j(x)=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). Hence \(\Delta q(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x)-P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and, under weak selection monotonicity, \(m(x)=P(S_0=S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). If \(\Delta q(x)>0\), then \(d(x)=+1\); if \(\Delta q(x)<0\), then \(d(x)=-1\). No direction is identified from the observable gap when \(\Delta q(x)=0\).
statements.justification: This projection converts observed IV contrasts into the two latent submargins needed for transport.
statements.gap: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 targets a survivor-complier mean, and DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 with equations (3.1)--(3.2) partitions weak selection directions for trimmed mean bounds; neither identifies the two ordinal submeasures as capacities for a same-unit coupling.
statements.consumer: An analyst can compute the survivor-complier outcome capacities directly from the Job Corps instrument, treatment, employment, and categorized-wage cells.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_x>0\).  Instrument overlap makes conditioning on \((Z=z,X=x)\) well defined for both \(z\).  Treatment consistency, selection exclusion-consistency, and outcome exclusion-consistency give
\[
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=i,S=1,D=0\mid Z=z,X=x)
=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_z=0\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
Conditional instrument independence removes \(Z=z\) from the right side.  Hence, by the definition of \(\ell_i(x)\),
\[
\ell_i(x)=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_0=0\mid X=x)-P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_1=0\mid X=x).
\]
No defiers gives \(D_1\ge D_0\), so \(\{D_1=0\}\subseteq\{D_0=0\}\), and the difference is
\[
P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_0=0,D_1=1\mid X=x)=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,C\mid X=x).
\]
The symmetric calculation uses \(\{D_0=1\}\subseteq\{D_1=1\}\) and yields
\[
h_j(x)=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,C\mid X=x).
\]
Summing over the finite support \(\mathcal Y\) proves
\[
q_0(x)=P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x),\qquad q_1(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x),
\]
and subtraction gives the asserted expression for \(\Delta q(x)\).

Under weak selection monotonicity, conditional on \((C,X=x)\), either \(S_1\ge S_0\) almost surely or \(S_1\le S_0\) almost surely.  In the first case,
\[
P(S_0=S_1=1,C\mid X=x)=P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x)=q_0(x)=m(x),
\]
and
\[
\Delta q(x)=P(S_0=0,S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\ge0.
\]
In the second case, the survivor mass is \(q_1(x)=m(x)\) and
\[
\Delta q(x)=-P(S_0=1,S_1=0,C\mid X=x)\le0.
\]
Thus a positive gap forces \(d(x)=+1\), a negative gap forces \(d(x)=-1\), and a zero gap does not identify the label.  Indeed, at zero gap either permitted monotonicity direction makes its one-sided selection stratum have probability zero.

statements.statement: For every supported cell, \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}\) if and only if \(\Delta q(x)=0\). On this tie face, weak selection monotonicity implies \(P(S_0=S_1,C\mid X=x)=P(C\mid X=x)\), and \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}=\Gamma_x\): in \(\Gamma_x^{+}\), the column inequalities bind because their total capacity equals the required row mass, and symmetrically the row inequalities bind in \(\Gamma_x^{-}\). Moreover, \(\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)=h_{>t}(x)-\ell_{>t}(x)\) for every \(t\), so the increasing, decreasing, and explicit tie formulas for \(B_L(x)\) coincide, while all three branches share \(B_U(x)\).
statements.justification: The zero-gap face must be identified without assigning an artificial observable sign to a latent weak-monotonicity direction.
statements.gap: DongHeiler2026 equations (3.1)--(3.2) attach the no-selection intersection to one directional partition by convention; this proposition instead proves that the projected coupling geometry is direction-invariant exactly on that intersection.
statements.consumer: Implementations can evaluate zero selection-effect cells deterministically through the fixed-marginal branch and avoid an arbitrary sign convention.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppress \(x\) and write \(q_0=\sum_i\ell_i\), \(q_1=\sum_jh_j\), and \(m=\min\{q_0,q_1\}\).  The exact-mass definition gives, for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}\),
\[
\sum_i\left(\ell_i-\sum_j\gamma_{ij}\right)=q_0-m,
\qquad
\sum_j\left(h_j-\sum_i\gamma_{ij}\right)=q_1-m.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative.  If \(q_0<q_1\), the first sum is zero, so every row constraint binds and \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^+\).  If \(q_1<q_0\), every column constraint binds and \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^-\).  If \(q_0=q_1=m\), both sums vanish, whence
\[
\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^+=\Gamma_x^-=\Gamma_x^0.
\]
Conversely, if \(q_0\ne q_1\), a matrix cannot have both exact margins, because its total mass cannot equal both unequal totals.  The smaller-margin directional polytope is nonempty by a greedy complete-bipartite allocation, whereas \(\Gamma_x^0\) is empty.  Therefore \(\Gamma_x^+=\Gamma_x^-=\Gamma_x^0\) holds if and only if \(\Delta q(x)=0\), and on that face it also equals \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).

By capacity identification and weak selection monotonicity, a zero gap makes the probability of the permitted one-sided selection stratum equal to zero.  Hence \(S_0=S_1\) almost surely among compliers in the cell and
\[
P(S_0=S_1,C\mid X=x)=P(C\mid X=x).
\]
Finally, when \(q_0=q_1\), for every \(t\),
\[
\ell_{\le t}-h_{\le t}
=(q_0-\ell_{>t})-(q_1-h_{>t})
=h_{>t}-\ell_{>t}.
\]
Also \(\min\{\Delta q,0\}=0\).  Thus the branch-free lower formula equals both legacy directional formulas, and the upper formula is common to all presentations.

statements.statement: For every \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) compatible with \(\mathcal M\), the threshold-flow construction returns full laws \(P^L\) and \(P^U\) over \((Y_0,Y_1,S_0,S_1,D_0,D_1,X,Z)\) that belong to \(\mathcal M\), induce exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and obey \(P^L(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_L\) and \(P^U(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_U\), including observable tie cells and zero-survivor cells.
statements.justification: A full latent completion is required for sharpness because locally feasible couplings need not automatically paste into one IV law.
statements.gap: deAguasEtAl2025 Propositions 4--5 attain ordered-benefit bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals, and GabrielSachsJensen2024 obtains symbolic latent-response bounds; neither lifts an extremal coupling of unequal survivor-complier submeasures to a full law satisfying the IV, compliance, and selection restrictions.
statements.consumer: Sensitivity and simulation work can use the attaining laws as exact least-favorable data-generating processes rather than generic linear-program certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose a baseline compatible law \(\bar P\in\mathcal M\), whose existence is part of compatibility.  The sharp-threshold theorem and compactness give, for each cell, \(\gamma_x^L,\gamma_x^U\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}\) such that
\[
b_x(\gamma_x^L)=B_L(x),\qquad b_x(\gamma_x^U)=B_U(x).
\]
When \(m(x)=0\), both matrices are the zero matrix.  We apply the same completion separately to the lower and upper collections.

Fix one selected matrix \(\gamma_x\).  Its total mass is \(m(x)\).  If \(q_1(x)>q_0(x)\), the row-slack sum is \(q_0(x)-m(x)=0\), so every row binds.  The column residuals
\[
r_j=h_j(x)-\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}
\]
are nonnegative and sum to \(q_1(x)-q_0(x)\).  Allocate them to compliers with \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\) and \(Y_1=j\), and allocate the remaining complier mass \(P(C\mid X=x)-q_1(x)\ge0\) to \((0,0)\).  If \(q_0(x)>q_1(x)\), every column binds; allocate the row residuals
\[
r_i=\ell_i(x)-\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}
\]
to \((S_0,S_1)=(1,0)\) compliers with \(Y_0=i\), and put the remaining mass \(P(C\mid X=x)-q_0(x)\) in \((0,0)\).  At equality both margins bind and all nonsurviving compliers use \((0,0)\).  These checks also cover zero-survivor cells.  Assign arbitrary potential outcomes whenever the corresponding selection indicator is zero.

For each endpoint construction retain from \(\bar P\) the law of \(X\), the conditional probabilities of the three no-defier compliance types, and every never-taker and always-taker latent component.  Replace only the conditional complier selection/outcome allocation by the preceding one.  Retain \(P(Z=1\mid X=x)=\pi(x)\), draw \(Z\) conditionally independently of all potential variables, and set \(D=D_Z\), \(S=S_D\), and \(Y=Y_D\) on \(\{S=1\}\).  Conditional instrument independence, all consistency and exclusion restrictions, overlap, and no defiers then hold by construction.  The allocation uses only \((1,1),(0,1),(0,0)\) when \(q_1>q_0\), only \((1,1),(1,0),(0,0)\) when \(q_0>q_1\), and only \((1,1),(0,0)\) at equality, so weak selection monotonicity also holds.

The selected complier outcome masses under treatment zero and one are exactly \(\ell\) and \(h\); all noncomplier observed components are unchanged.  The resulting laws therefore induce exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Call the lower and upper completions \(P^L\) and \(P^U\).  Their common target-stratum mass is \(M>0\), while
\[
P^L(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xB_L(x),
\]
and
\[
P^U(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xB_U(x).
\]
Division by \(M\) gives \(\theta_L\) and \(\theta_U\), respectively.  This is a full-law attainment argument, not merely attainment inside the projected transport polytope.

statements.statement: The displayed latent allocation defines \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M\) and induces exactly the fully specified law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\): every unit is a complier, weak selection monotonicity holds in the increasing direction, and the selected cells under each instrument arm equal the listed probabilities. Applying the observable contrasts to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\) gives \(\ell=(0.075,0.10,0.075)\), \(h=(0.10,0.25,0.15)\), \(q_0=m=0.25\), \(q_1=0.50\), and \(\Delta q=0.25\). The threshold cuts then give \(B_L=0\) and \(B_U=0.175\); consequently the sharpness and full-law-attainment theorems imply \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star})=[0,0.7]\) and attainment of both endpoints.
statements.justification: The witness separates survivor share, selected-arm mixture, and same-unit coupling uncertainty in the smallest informative ordered support.
statements.gap: ChenFlores2015 reports mean wage-effect bounds for always-employed Job Corps compliers, while deAguasEtAl2025 studies ordered-tier benefit from complete treatment-arm marginals; neither displays an IV-selection witness with unequal capacities and endpoint-attaining full laws.
statements.consumer: The witness is a reproducible diagnostic for software and a transparent calibration for the Job Corps reinterpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
The displayed latent masses are nonnegative and sum to
\[
0.075+0.10+0.075+0.25+0.50=1.
\]
Every unit has \((D_0,D_1)=(0,1)\), so every unit is a complier and there are no defiers.  The only selection types are \((1,1),(0,1),(0,0)\), so weak selection monotonicity holds in the increasing direction.  The fair instrument is independent of all potential variables, and the imposed consistency and exclusion rules give, under \(Z=0\), selected outcome masses \((0.075,0.10,0.075)\) at \(D=0\) and unselected mass \(0.75\).  Under \(Z=1\), the selected masses at \(D=1\) are
\[
(0.075,0.10,0.075)+(0.025,0.15,0.075)=(0.10,0.25,0.15),
\]
with unselected mass \(0.50\).  Thus \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M\) and it induces exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\).

Capacity identification gives
\[
\ell=(0.075,0.10,0.075),\qquad h=(0.10,0.25,0.15),
\]
so \(q_0=m=0.25\), \(q_1=0.50\), and \(\Delta q=0.25\).  The prefix differences \(\ell_{\le t}-h_{\le t}\) are \(-0.025,-0.175,-0.25\), and \(\min\{\Delta q,0\}=0\); hence the branch-free lower formula gives \(B_L=0\).  The upper threshold values \(\ell_{<t}+h_{>t}\), for \(t=0,1,2\), are
\[
0.40,\qquad0.225,\qquad0.175.
\]
Taking their minimum together with the mass cap \(m=0.25\) gives \(B_U=0.175\).  The sharp theorem therefore yields
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star})=\left[\frac0{0.25},\frac{0.175}{0.25}\right]=[0,0.7].
\]

The displayed diagonal survivor allocation attains the lower endpoint.  For the upper endpoint, send mass \(0.075\) from \(Y_0=0\) to \(Y_1=1\), mass \(0.10\) from \(Y_0=1\) to \(Y_1=2\), and mass \(0.075\) from \(Y_0=2\) to \(Y_1=0\).  Its row margin is \(\ell\), its column usage is \((0.075,0.075,0.10)\le h\), its total is \(m\), and its benefit mass is \(0.175\).  Allocating the residual columns \((0.025,0.175,0.05)\) to \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\) completes an upper endpoint law.  Thus both endpoints are attained by explicit full latent laws.

statements.statement: On the no-selection submodel with \(P(S_0=S_1=1\mid C,X=x)=1\) for each cell with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\), one has \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{0}\), the full coupling polytope for the identified survivor-complier marginals \(\ell(x)/m(x)\) and \(h(x)/m(x)\). After division by \(m(x)\), \(B_L(x)\) and \(B_U(x)\) equal the sharp fixed-marginal strict-benefit formulas in LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), cell by cell.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that partial transport nests classical fixed-marginal benefit bounds.
statements.gap: LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), establishes the complete-marginal formula; this theorem proves its exact equivalence to the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) face recovered from the IV-selection model.
statements.consumer: Users can verify implementations against a published closed form whenever selection disappears.
statements.proof_tex:
\noindent\textit{Proof.}
Fix a supported cell \(x\), and write \(c_x=P(C\mid X=x)\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}capacity\text{-}identification}\), whose premises include conditional instrument independence, instrument overlap, and no defiers, gives
\[
q_0(x)=P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x),
\qquad
q_1(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x).
\]
If \(c_x=0\), both displayed probabilities vanish because their events are subsets of \(C\).  Moreover, every \(\ell_i(x)\) and every \(h_j(x)\) vanishes by the same proposition.  Consequently
\[
q_0(x)=q_1(x)=m(x)=\Delta q(x)=0,
\qquad
\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^{0}=\{0\},
\qquad
B_L(x)=B_U(x)=0.
\]
There is no normalized survivor-complier distribution in this zero-mass cell, so every division below is restricted to \(c_x>0\), exactly as required by the conditional statement of the theorem.

Now suppose \(c_x>0\).  The no-selection restriction states
\[
P(S_0=S_1=1\mid C,X=x)=1.
\]
Since \(\{S_0=S_1=1\}\subseteq\{S_d=1\}\) for \(d\in\{0,1\}\), this restriction and the probability-one upper bound imply
\[
P(S_d=1\mid C,X=x)=1,
\qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Multiplying by the positive conditioning mass \(c_x\) yields
\[
P(S_d=1,C\mid X=x)=c_x,
\qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Substitution in the capacity-identification equalities therefore gives
\[
q_0(x)=q_1(x)=c_x,
\qquad
\Delta q(x)=q_1(x)-q_0(x)=0,
\qquad
m(x)=\min\{q_0(x),q_1(x)\}=c_x>0.
\]
Thus Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}tie\text{-}face\text{-}collapse}\) already implies \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{0}\).  For completeness, the binding argument can be read directly from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}partial\text{-}transport\text{-}polytope}\).  If \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{\ast}\), define its row and column sums by
\[
r_i=\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x},
\qquad
s_j=\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}.
\]
The defining inequalities give \(0\le r_i\le\ell_i(x)\) and \(0\le s_j\le h_j(x)\), while exact mass and the preceding equalities give
\[
\sum_i r_i=m(x)=q_0(x)=\sum_i\ell_i(x),
\qquad
\sum_j s_j=m(x)=q_1(x)=\sum_jh_j(x).
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_i\bigl(\ell_i(x)-r_i\bigr)=0,
\qquad
\sum_j\bigl(h_j(x)-s_j\bigr)=0.
\]
Every summand in these two finite sums is nonnegative, so every summand equals zero.  Therefore \(r_i=\ell_i(x)\) for all \(i\) and \(s_j=h_j(x)\) for all \(j\), proving \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x^{0}\).  Conversely, every \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x^{0}\) satisfies the two capacity inequalities and has total mass
\[
\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij,x}=\sum_i\ell_i(x)=m(x),
\]
so it belongs to \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x\).  This proves
\[
\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^{0}.
\]

Because \(m(x)>0\), define the normalized cumulative distribution functions
\[
F_0(t)=\frac{\ell_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)},
\qquad
F_1(t)=\frac{h_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)},
\qquad
F_0(-1)=0.
\]
The capacity totals equal \(m(x)\), so \(\ell_i(x)/m(x)\) and \(h_j(x)/m(x)\) are probability mass functions on the finite ordered support \(\mathcal Y\).  Moreover, the scaling map
\[
\gamma_x\longmapsto \gamma_x/m(x)
\]
is a bijection from \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) onto the complete coupling polytope having those two marginals; its inverse multiplies a probability coupling by \(m(x)\).

Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}threshold\text{-}cuts}\), together with \(\Delta q(x)=0\), gives
\[
\frac{B_L(x)}{m(x)}
=\max\left\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}
\frac{\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)}\right\}
=\max\left\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl(F_0(t)-F_1(t)\bigr)\right\}.
\]
For the upper endpoint, \(\ell_{<t}(x)/m(x)=F_0(t-1)\) and \(h_{>t}(x)/m(x)=1-F_1(t)\), whence
\[
\frac{B_U(x)}{m(x)}
=\min\left\{1,\min_{t\in\mathcal Y}
\bigl(F_0(t-1)+1-F_1(t)\bigr)\right\}.
\]
At \(t=0\), the inner expression is \(h_{>0}(x)/m(x)\le1\).  Thus the separate cap by one is redundant and
\[
\frac{B_U(x)}{m(x)}
=\min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl(F_0(t-1)+1-F_1(t)\bigr)
=\min_{t\in\mathcal Y}
\frac{\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)}{m(x)}.
\]
The revalidated cited Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinal\text{-}fixed\text{-}marginal\text{-}strict\text{-}benefit}\), which is Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta's Proposition 2, equation (6), states that these are exactly the sharp lower and upper probabilities of \(Y_1>Y_0\) over all couplings of the two normalized ordinal marginals.  The scaling bijection therefore identifies \(B_L(x)/m(x)\) and \(B_U(x)/m(x)\) with the published fixed-marginal strict-benefit endpoints, cell by cell. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Can the near-active-face directional-multiplier handle be calibrated so that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\}\ge1-\alpha,\] uniformly over direction-separated triangular arrays \(\mathcal P_n\), while allowing arbitrary simultaneous threshold-cut ties and covariate cells whose survivor mass approaches zero and is omitted at the unnormalized threshold \(\eta_n\)?
statements.justification: Uniform simultaneous coverage at intersecting cut and zero-mass faces is the proposal's genuine unresolved inferential content.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 handles estimated directional derivatives, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 handles localized contact sets, Semenova2025 handles covariate-specific Lee directions, and deAguasEtAl2025 equations (17)--(18) give pointwise stabilized coverage for tier-benefit bounds. None establishes uniform joint validity for two summed survivor-complier transport endpoints with changing cell support.
statements.consumer: The result would deliver an honest confidence set for the complete sharp Job Corps benefit interval even when several wage thresholds bind.

statements.statement: Under independent sampling from a probability law on a fixed finite support, the empirical probability vector satisfies a multivariate central limit theorem: its centered \(\sqrt n\)-scaled error converges to a mean-zero Gaussian vector with the multinomial covariance matrix.

statements.statement:
Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) be induced by at least one law in \(\mathcal M\).  For every supported cell,
\[
\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x),\ \sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij,x}=m(x)\right\}
\]
is exactly the projection of all compatible laws onto the survivor-complier coupling.  Exact mass forces the smaller-total margin to bind: \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^{+}\) if \(\Delta q(x)>0\), \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^{-}\) if \(\Delta q(x)<0\), and \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\Gamma_x^{0}\) if \(\Delta q(x)=0\).  Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}}b_x(\gamma_x)
=\max\left\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)\bigr]+\min\{\Delta q(x),0\}\right\}=B_L(x),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}}b_x(\gamma_x)
=\min\left\{m(x),\min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)\bigr]\right\}=B_U(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\left[\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xB_L(x)}{M},\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xB_U(x)}{M}\right],
\]
and this interval is sharp; cells with \(m(x)=0\) contribute the unique zero coupling.
statements.justification: A single exact-mass capacity polytope and nested cuts turn unequal observed submeasures into closed sharp benefit endpoints without observable sign dispatch.
statements.gap: Complete-marginal ordinal-benefit formulas do not solve the unequal survivor-complier submeasure problem induced jointly by noncompliance and treatment-dependent selection.
statements.consumer: A policy evaluator obtains the sharp fraction of always-employed compliers whose ordered outcome rises from one branch-free observable map.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a supported cell and suppress \(x\).  Put \(a_i=\ell_i\), \(c_j=h_j\), and \(m=\min\{\sum_i a_i,\sum_jc_j\}\).  We first derive the finite flow identity used below.  For a bipartite edge set \(E\), let \(F(E;a,c)\) be the greatest mass of a nonnegative flow supported on \(E\), with row capacities \(a\) and column capacities \(c\).  For every row set \(A\), splitting flow according as its row lies outside \(A\) or inside \(A\) gives
\[
F(E;a,c)\le a(\mathcal Y\setminus A)+c(N_E(A)).
\tag{1}
\]
To prove equality for some cut, choose a maximum flow, which exists because the feasible capacity box is compact.  In its residual network let \(A\) be the rows reachable from the source and let \(N_E(A)\) be the reachable columns.  No augmenting path exists.  Consequently every source arc entering \(\mathcal Y\setminus A\) and every sink arc leaving \(N_E(A)\) is saturated; otherwise the corresponding endpoint would be reachable.  Flow conservation, including reverse residual arcs, then makes (1) an equality.  Thus
\[
F(E;a,c)=\min_{A\subseteq\mathcal Y}\{a(\mathcal Y\setminus A)+c(N_E(A))\}.
\tag{2}
\]

For benefit edges \(E_< =\{(i,j):i<j\}\), a nonempty \(A\) with \(t=\min A\) has \(N_{E_<}(A)=\{j:j>t\}\); at fixed \(t\), the cut is minimized by \(A=\{i:i\ge t\}\).  The empty row set and the analogous all-column cut supply the two total-capacity cuts.  Hence
\[
F(E_<;a,c)=\min\left\{m,\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}(a_{<t}+c_{>t})\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For nonbenefit edges \(E_{\ge}=\{(i,j):j\le i\}\), the same argument with \(t=\max A\) gives
\[
F(E_{\ge};a,c)=\min\left\{m,\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}(a_{>t}+c_{\le t})\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]

Any subflow of mass \(f\le m\) can be extended to total mass \(m\) on the complete bipartite graph: after subtracting the subflow, both the total residual row capacity and the total residual column capacity are at least \(m-f\), and a two-pointer greedy allocation sends precisely that amount.  Apply this to a maximum benefit subflow.  If its mass is below \(m\), no residual benefit edge can carry positive flow, since that would augment the subflow.  Therefore its completion has the same benefit mass, and (3) proves
\[
\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}}b_x(\gamma)
=\min\left\{m,\min_t(\ell_{<t}+h_{>t})\right\}=B_U(x).
\tag{5}
\]
Next complete a maximum nonbenefit subflow.  If its mass is below \(m\), every added unit is beneficial by the same residual-edge argument.  Thus (4) yields
\[
\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}}b_x(\gamma)
=m-F(E_{\ge};\ell,h)
=\max\left\{0,\max_t(m-\ell_{>t}-h_{\le t})\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Since \(q_0=\ell_{\le t}+\ell_{>t}\) and \(m-q_0=\min\{q_1-q_0,0\}=\min\{\Delta q,0\}\),
\[
m-\ell_{>t}-h_{\le t}
=\ell_{\le t}-h_{\le t}+\min\{\Delta q,0\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) are exactly the branch-free formula for \(B_L(x)\).  The nonnegative row and column slack identities in the tie-face proof show simultaneously that \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\) recovers \(\Gamma_x^+\), \(\Gamma_x^-\), and \(\Gamma_x^0\) in the positive, negative, and zero-gap cases.

It remains to prove that this observable optimization equals the causal identified set.  Let \(\bar P\in\mathcal M\) induce \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Capacity identification and weak selection monotonicity imply that its survivor-complier subcoupling has row sums bounded by \(\ell\), column sums bounded by \(h\), and total mass \(m\); it therefore lies in \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).  Conversely, fix \(\gamma\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).  If \(q_1>q_0\), exact mass forces every row to bind.  Assign \(\gamma_{ij}\) to survivor compliers with outcomes \((i,j)\), assign
\[
h_j-\sum_i\gamma_{ij}\ge0
\]
to \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\) compliers with \(Y_1=j\), and assign the remaining complier mass \(P(C\mid X=x)-q_1\ge0\) to \((0,0)\).  If \(q_0>q_1\), exact columns bind; assign \(\ell_i-\sum_j\gamma_{ij}\) to \((1,0)\) compliers with \(Y_0=i\), and put mass \(P(C\mid X=x)-q_0\) in \((0,0)\).  On a tie both margins bind and all nonsurviving compliers use \((0,0)\).  Nonnegativity follows from the capacity constraints, while the final remainders are nonnegative because \(q_d=P(S_d=1,C\mid X=x)\le P(C\mid X=x)\).  Assign arbitrary outcomes where selection is zero and retain all noncomplier components of \(\bar P\).  This preserves the two selected-complier submargins, every noncomplier observed component, the instrument propensity, and every maintained restriction.  Thus every \(\gamma\in\Gamma_x^{\ast}\) is the projection of a compatible full law.

The construction is independent across the finite cells.  For every compatible law,
\[
P(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xb_x(\gamma_x),
\qquad
P(S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xm(x)=M.
\]
The positive-aggregate-survivor assumption permits division by \(M\).  The finite product of the compact convex polytopes \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\) is compact and convex, and the numerator is linear, so its image is the entire closed interval between its summed cellwise extrema.  A cell with \(m(x)=0\) has only the zero coupling.  Dividing (5)--(7) by \(M\) proves the stated equality for \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), including sharpness rather than merely an outer bound.

statements.statement: For finite \(\mathcal X\) and \(K\), the branch-free threshold formulas and sparse lower- and upper-attaining couplings in \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\) can be computed using \(O(|\mathcal X|K)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons.  If every entry of each dense \(K\times K\) coupling matrix must be materialized, the complexity is \(O(|\mathcal X|K^2)\).  Both operation counts are independent of the numerical magnitudes of the capacities.
statements.justification: The nested Ferrers geometry yields a genuinely linear scan when couplings are stored sparsely.
statements.gap: Symbolic latent-response linear programs and stabilized complete-marginal estimators do not provide magnitude-free linear-time sparse coupling construction for unequal submeasures.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers can recompute exact bounds across bootstrap draws and discretizations without solving a latent-type linear program.
statements.proof_tex:
For each cell, compute the prefix sums of \(\ell\) and \(h\), the complementary tails, \(q_0,q_1,m\), and \(\Delta q\) in one forward and one backward scan.  A scan over the \(K\) thresholds then evaluates the branch-free maximum for \(B_L\) and the minimum for \(B_U\).  This uses \(O(K)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons.

For a sparse upper-attaining coupling, compute a maximum flow on the Ferrers graph \(i<j\).  Process columns in increasing order and supply each from the largest-index residual row satisfying \(i<j\), keeping eligible residual rows on a stack.  Each row is pushed once, each exhausted row is popped once, and each assignment exhausts a row or a column.  An exchange proves maximality: if a more restrictive, larger row is sent to a later column while a less restrictive row supplies an earlier column, swapping the smaller assigned mass preserves feasibility and does not decrease benefit flow.  Iterating leaves the stated greedy order.  Thus the scan uses \(O(K)\) operations and emits at most \(2K-1\) positive assignments.

For a maximum nonbenefit subflow on \(j\le i\), reverse the order: process columns from high to low and supply them from the smallest-index eligible residual row.  The identical nested-neighborhood exchange argument proves maximality, with the same linear bound.  Extend either maximum subflow to exact mass \(m\) by a two-pointer complete-bipartite scan on its residual row and column capacities.  Each completion assignment again exhausts a row or a column, so it costs \(O(K)\) and has \(O(K)\) support.  If the maximum benefit subflow has mass below \(m\), no residual benefit edge exists; hence its completion attains \(B_U\).  If the maximum nonbenefit subflow has mass below \(m\), no residual nonbenefit edge exists; hence its completion leaves exactly \(B_L\) on benefit arcs.  These are the cut equalities established in the sharp-threshold theorem.

Therefore endpoints and sparse attaining couplings cost \(O(K)\) per cell and \(O(|\mathcal X|K)\) overall.  Initializing or writing every entry of dense \(K\times K\) arrays itself costs \(O(K^2)\) per cell and dominates the scans, giving \(O(|\mathcal X|K^2)\).  No loop count depends on any capacity magnitude, so both bounds are strongly polynomial in the stated arithmetic/comparison model.

statements.statement:
Fix a finite-support law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) induced by some \(P\in\mathcal M\) and satisfying instrument overlap, independent sampling, and \(M>0\).  No direction-separation condition is required.  Then
\[
P\!\left\{\{x:\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}=\mathcal X_+(P)\right\}\to1,\qquad
\widehat\Psi_n\to_P\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\) converges to \(\mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) passed through the Hadamard directional derivative of the following reduced-support composite map: coordinatewise projection onto \(\mathfrak C\); the branch-free lower functional
\[
\max\left\{0,\max_t[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)]+\min\{\Delta q(x),0\}\right\};
\]
the upper minimum over the mass cap and threshold cuts; and the \(p_x\)-weighted common-denominator quotient.  At \(\Delta q(x)=0\), the lower derivative uses the active face \(g\mapsto\min\{\Delta q_x'(g),0\}\), while the mass-cap derivative uses \(g\mapsto\min\{q_{0,x}'(g),q_{1,x}'(g)\}\).  Thus positive-survivor zero-gap cells and arbitrary simultaneous threshold ties are included.  Zero-survivor cells contribute zero because screening recovers the fixed reduced support with probability tending to one.
statements.justification: The branch-free min/max representation exposes the exact directional derivative at positive-survivor zero-gap cells and removes an artificial direction margin.
statements.gap: Generic directional delta methods do not derive the composed capacity projection, exact-mass cuts, screening, and ratio derivative for these survivor-complier endpoints.
statements.consumer: A practitioner obtains the correct non-Gaussian fixed-law limit even when the two selected-complier masses tie.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(v\) be the finite vector of observed atomic probabilities and \(\widehat v_n\) its empirical vector.  Independent sampling and the established finite multinomial central limit theorem give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat v_n-v)\rightsquigarrow\mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}.
\tag{1}
\]
For a fixed supported cell, overlap makes both \((X=x,Z=z)\) denominators positive.  The map from \(v\) to the raw capacity contrasts is therefore continuously differentiable at this law.

The projection onto \(\mathfrak C\) is coordinatewise positive part and has Hadamard directional derivative
\[
[\Pi_{\mathfrak C}'(g)]_k=
\begin{cases}
g_k,&c_k>0,\\
\max\{g_k,0\},&c_k=0.
\end{cases}
\tag{2}
\]
All subsequent maps are finite maxima or minima of affine maps.  Write
\[
A_{x,t}=\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x),\quad
G_x=\max_t A_{x,t},\quad
s_x=\min\{\Delta q(x),0\}.
\]
Then \(B_L(x)=\max\{0,G_x+s_x\}\).  Direct first-order expansion of a finite maximum gives
\[
G_x'(g)=\max_{t:A_{x,t}=G_x}A_{x,t}'(g).
\tag{3}
\]
For the active minimum,
\[
s_x'(g)=
\begin{cases}
\Delta q_x'(g),&\Delta q(x)<0,\\
0,&\Delta q(x)>0,\\
\min\{\Delta q_x'(g),0\},&\Delta q(x)=0.
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
The outer positive part has derivative equal to \(G_x'(g)+s_x'(g)\) when \(G_x+s_x>0\), zero when that quantity is negative, and \(\max\{G_x'(g)+s_x'(g),0\}\) on its zero face.  This is the maximum over the active lower cuts, including the zero cut, with the active minimum face in (4).

For the upper endpoint, put \(U_{x,t}=\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)\).  Since
\[
B_U(x)=\min\{m(x),U_{x,0},\ldots,U_{x,K-1}\},
\]
its derivative is the minimum of the derivatives of all active entries.  In particular,
\[
m_x'(g)=
\begin{cases}
q_{0,x}'(g),&q_0(x)<q_1(x),\\
q_{1,x}'(g),&q_1(x)<q_0(x),\\
\min\{q_{0,x}'(g),q_{1,x}'(g)\},&q_0(x)=q_1(x).
\end{cases}
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) explicitly include positive-survivor zero-gap cells and require no locally fixed sign branch.

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let \(N_e=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_+(P)}p_xB_e(x)\).  The quotient derivative is
\[
\left(\frac{N_e}{M}\right)'(g)=\frac{N_e'(g)M-N_eM'(g)}{M^2},
\tag{6}
\]
which is well defined because \(M>0\).

It remains to justify the reduced support.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal X\) gives a positive minimum of \(r_x=p_xm(x)\) over \(\mathcal X_+(P)\), so consistency and \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) retain every such cell with probability tending to one.  If \(p_x=0\), then \(\widehat p_x=0\) almost surely.  If \(p_x>0\) and \(m(x)=0\), one of the nonnegative population capacity vectors has every coordinate zero.  The smooth first stage and (2) imply \(\widehat m(x)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and hence
\[
\widehat r_x=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\eta_n)
\]
because \(\sqrt n\eta_n\to\infty\).  A finite union proves exact screened-support recovery.

The composite map described by (2)--(6) is Hadamard directionally differentiable.  Applying the established directional delta method to (1), then using support recovery to replace the screened map by the fixed reduced-support map with probability tending to one, proves the asserted limit.  The same composition with the unscaled law of large numbers proves consistency.

statements.statement:
Set \(a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\) and
\[
g_n=\frac{512K|\mathcal X|}{m_{\star}\varepsilon_Z^2}(a_n+\eta_n).
\]
Define
\[
\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}
=\left[\max\{0,\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_n\},\ \min\{1,\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_n\}\right].
\]
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\),
\[
P\!\left\{\|\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\|_\infty\le g_n\right\}\to1
\]
and therefore
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\}\to1.
\]
This uniformly consistent conservative conclusion permits arbitrary simultaneous threshold-cut ties, positive-survivor zero-gap cells, and survivor masses approaching zero that are omitted at \(\eta_n\).  Its validity is supplied entirely by the deterministic guard; it does not assert first-order exact calibration of an unguarded face-aware multiplier confidence set.
statements.justification: A finite-cell concentration bound and an explicit vanishing guard deliver uniform full-set containment without claiming unsupported multiplier calibration.
statements.gap: First-order exact uniform calibration of an unguarded estimated-face multiplier remains unresolved; the proved result is deliberately conservative.
statements.consumer: Users obtain a computable uniformly consistent confidence set robust to cut ties, zero-gap cells, and changing survivor support.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal E\) be the fixed finite collection of observed atomic and aggregate cell events needed for all empirical conditional probabilities, and define
\[
\delta_n=\max_{E\in\mathcal E}|\widehat P_n(E)-P_{\mathrm{obs}}(E)|.
\]
For each indicator, independence gives variance at most \(1/(4n)\).  Since \(\mathbf 1\{|W|>u\}\le W^2/u^2\), taking expectations and summing over \(\mathcal E\) yields, uniformly in \(P\),
\[
P(\delta_n>u)\le\frac{|\mathcal E|}{4nu^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
Now \(a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\downarrow0\) and
\[
na_n^2=\sqrt{n/\eta_n}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
so (1) implies \(\delta_n/a_n\to_P0\) uniformly.

We compare unconditional capacities.  Put \(L_i(x)=p_x\ell_i(x)\), \(H_j(x)=p_xh_j(x)\), \(\widehat L_i(x)=\widehat p_x\widehat\ell_i(x)\), and \(\widehat H_j(x)=\widehat p_x\widehat h_j(x)\).  On a cell satisfying \(p_x\ge4\delta_n/\varepsilon_Z\), overlap gives population denominators at least \(\varepsilon_Zp_x\), while their empirical counterparts are at least half that value.  Expanding each empirical ratio, using that every numerator is bounded by its denominator, and then taking the difference of the two instrument arms gives
\[
\max_{i,j}\{|\widehat L_i(x)-L_i(x)|,|\widehat H_j(x)-H_j(x)|\}
\le\frac{16\delta_n}{\varepsilon_Z^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
The coordinatewise positive-part projection does not enlarge this bound because \(p_x\ell_i(x)\) and \(p_xh_j(x)\) are nonnegative and \(\widehat p_x\max\{u,0\}=\max\{\widehat p_xu,0\}\).  If \(p_x<4\delta_n/\varepsilon_Z\), both population unconditional capacities are at most \(p_x\), both empirical unconditional capacities are at most \(\widehat p_x\le p_x+\delta_n\), and (2), with its larger constant, still holds.  Thus (2) is valid for every cell on the event defining \(\delta_n\).

The branch-free cut functionals are positively homogeneous.  If every unconditional capacity coordinate changes by at most \(e\), each prefix or tail changes by at most \(Ke\), \(\Delta q\) by at most \(2Ke\), and the lower and upper cut values by at most \(4Ke\).  Therefore the unscreened aggregate numerator and denominator errors are each at most
\[
A_{0,n}=\frac{64K|\mathcal X|}{\varepsilon_Z^2}\delta_n.
\tag{3}
\]
This Lipschitz calculation uses no sign classification and is valid at every simultaneous threshold tie and every zero-gap face.

Screening removes only cells with estimated unconditional survivor mass \(\widehat r_x\le\eta_n\).  Since \(0\le\widehat B_L(x)\le\widehat B_U(x)\le\widehat m(x)\), deleting all such cells changes each empirical numerator and the empirical denominator by at most \(|\mathcal X|\eta_n\).  Consequently, for \(e=L,U\),
\[
|\widehat N_{e,n}-N_e|\le A_n,
\qquad
|\widehat M_n-M|\le A_n,
\qquad
A_n=A_{0,n}+|\mathcal X|\eta_n.
\tag{4}
\]
This argument directly covers cells whose survivor mass approaches zero and does not require uniform recovery of their support.

Because \(M\ge m_{\star}\), on \(A_n\le m_{\star}/2\) one has \(\widehat M_n\ge m_{\star}/2\), so the fallback is not used.  Since \(0\le N_e\le M\), elementary quotient algebra and (4) give
\[
\left|\frac{\widehat N_{e,n}}{\widehat M_n}-\frac{N_e}{M}\right|
\le\frac{|\widehat N_{e,n}-N_e|}{\widehat M_n}
+\frac{N_e|\widehat M_n-M|}{M\widehat M_n}
\le\frac{4A_n}{m_{\star}}.
\tag{5}
\]
On the event \(\delta_n\le a_n\), the right side of (5) is bounded by
\[
\frac{256K|\mathcal X|}{m_{\star}\varepsilon_Z^2}a_n
+\frac{4|\mathcal X|}{m_{\star}}\eta_n
\le g_n.
\tag{6}
\]
Equation (1) makes this event have probability tending to one uniformly, and \(A_n\le m_{\star}/2\) there eventually because \(a_n+\eta_n\to0\).  Equations (5)--(6) prove the asserted uniform consistency.

On \(\|\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\|_\infty\le g_n\), one has \(\theta_L\ge\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_n\) and \(\theta_U\le\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_n\).  The sharp-threshold theorem identifies \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), so the guarded interval contains the entire identified set.  Uniform containment probability therefore tends to one.  No multiplier quantile is used in this proof; calibration of an unguarded face-aware multiplier region remains an open strengthening.

For two distributions on \(\mathcal Y\) with masses \(\ell_i(x)/m(x)\) and \(h_j(x)/m(x)\), the sharp lower and upper bounds on the strict-benefit probability are
\[
\max\left\{0,\max_t\frac{\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)}\right\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min_t\frac{\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)}{m(x)},
\]
respectively.

sampling_model.design: Binary conditionally randomized or conditionally exogenous instrument \(Z\), with observational receipt \(D\) and treatment-induced selection \(S\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from a finite-cell superpopulation law.
sampling_model.treatment: Received treatment obeys \(D=D_Z\), no defiers, and exclusion through \(D\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical finite-cell conditional probabilities use zero when an empirical \(X,Z\) denominator vanishes. Their raw IV contrasts are projected in the fixed Euclidean metric onto \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), hence by coordinatewise positive part; cells are screened only through \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)>\eta_n\).

tldr: Observed instrument contrasts identify two possibly unequal selected-complier outcome submeasures in each covariate cell. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity makes their smaller total mass the survivor-complier mass; when the observable selection gap is zero, monotonicity forces selection equality among compliers and the two directional transport polytopes collapse to the same fixed-marginal tie face. Three-branch threshold cuts yield the sharp survivor-complier benefit interval, and a full-law construction attains both endpoints. A strongly polynomial algorithm, a fully specified compatible observed law with interval \([0,0.7]\), the classical fixed-marginal reduction, and a pointwise screened plug-in limit support the flagship identification result; uniform face-aware inference with changing survivor support remains open under a fixed direction margin.

project_justification.gap: DongHeiler2026 bounds survivor-complier means by trimming selected-complier distributions. LuDingDasgupta2018, GabrielSachsJensen2024, and deAguasEtAl2025 bound ordered benefit when complete treatment-arm marginals or different observable response-function restrictions are available. None characterizes the same-unit benefit probability from unequal survivor-complier submeasures induced jointly by noncompliance and treatment-dependent selection, including observable zero-gap cells.
project_justification.niche: Finite ordered outcomes make the strict-benefit graph a Ferrers network. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity turns the two observed submeasures into row or column capacities off the zero-gap face and into complete survivor-complier marginals on the zero-gap face.
project_justification.fill: The project derives explicit increasing, decreasing, and tie branches; proves the sharp partial-transport interval and full IV-selection-law endpoint attainment; supplies a strongly polynomial algorithm and a compatible one-cell observed-law witness with interval \([0,0.7]\); recovers the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta formula on \(\Gamma_x^{0}\); defines a total screened plug-in estimator and its fixed-law directional limit; and isolates uniform face-aware multiplier validity as an open question.

related_work: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 establishes survivor-complier mean effects under treatment-induced selection and provides the principal-stratum framing. ChenFlores2015 bounds mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers; the fully specified compatible witness here calibrates instead the fraction whose ordered wage category rises. DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 states cellwise weak sample-selection monotonicity, and equations (3.1)--(3.2) separate positive and negative direction cells while attaching the no-selection intersection to the positive partition by convention. Its sharp results concern intensive-margin means, so it informs the model but is not a theorem-level result being tightened. LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), gives the sharp strict-benefit interval from two complete ordinal marginals; the no-selection theorem makes that formula exactly the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) branch. GabrielSachsJensen2024 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 derive probability-of-benefit bounds under confounding and imperfect randomization by symbolic response-function methods, without treatment-induced survivor selection. deAguasEtAl2025 Definitions 1--2 define the same ordered-tier benefit event, Propositions 4--5 and equations (5)--(8) give sharp bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals under ignorability, and Section 5 with Algorithm 1 and equations (17)--(18) addresses nonregularity from tied complete-marginal bounds. That paper does not recover unequal survivor-complier submeasures under noncompliance and treatment-induced selection, derive directional partial-transport threshold formulas, or lift endpoint couplings to a compatible full IV-selection law. FangSantos2019 supplies directional resampling, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 supplies contact-set localization, and Semenova2025 studies covariate-specific Lee-bound directions; these sources motivate the fixed-law directional calculation and the separate open problem of uniform inference with estimated faces and changing survivor support.
technical_internal_limitation: Finite enumeration is evidence, not a proof. The early kill test enumerated denominator-five three-level capacity laws and solved the complier selection-type linear program with an explicit one-sided residual stratum. The linear-program endpoints agreed with the threshold formulas on 1,918 increasing-selection and 1,918 decreasing-selection laws, including 1,622 direction-specific checks on equal-total tie cases. The fully specified witness has an explicit compatible latent allocation and returns benefit masses \(0\) and \(0.175\), hence conditional endpoints \(0\) and \(0.7\). The general theorem still requires a symbolic endpoint-preserving completion for every compatible observed law. The pointwise directional limit does not by itself validate a confidence set.
honest_scope: The tie-safe capacity projection, three-branch threshold min-cut equality, full-law endpoint attainment, strongly polynomial construction, compatible three-level observed-law witness, fixed-marginal reduction, and fixed-law pointwise directional limit are theorem targets. Identification allows \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(m(x)=0\) and uses no direction margin. The pointwise limit imposes \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) only on the fixed positive-survivor support and screens zero-survivor cells with probability tending to one. Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, estimated near-active faces, and changing survivor support is explicitly open; rates for \(a_n\) and \(\eta_n\), critical-value calibration, uniform face recovery, and local-to-zero direction gaps are strengthening questions. No confidence-set validity, uniform inference, changing-support limit, or coverage under shrinking direction gaps is claimed. Continuous outcomes, monotonicity-violation sensitivity, and concordance restrictions are outside scope.
